steps.say: Many traders don't buy all at once. | They place a ladder of orders below the price, so a dip fills them at better prices.
The ladder helper sits right under the chart.
Choose long or short, and the kind of market. | Consolidating gives equal orders close to the price. | Trending makes the nearest order smallest and the furthest largest.
The orders are spaced by this coin's typical daily move, so a quiet coin gets a tight ladder and a wild one a wide ladder. | The stop sits beyond the last order.
Switch on Show on chart. | Blue lines for the orders, thicker for a bigger share, red for the stop, and grey for your average price if every order fills.

Or put the orders on Fibonacci levels. | Draw a Fibonacci from the swing low to the high, then choose On Fibonacci levels. | The orders move onto the retracement levels, and the stop goes just past the swing low. | With no drawing, it measures the last swing for you.
For the final entry, switch to five-minute candles. | They cover the last seven days, for crypto.
Switch the lines off when you're done.
